```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

sdvmodels ships the fitted models behind cfbfastR and the wider SportsDataverse
as data. Each model is the raw UBJ byte vector of the released file, so you load
it with `xgboost::xgb.load.raw()` and score it with `predict()`. Nothing is
downloaded at run time.

```{r}
library(sdvmodels)
library(xgboost)
```

## The feature contract

Every model expects its features in a fixed order. The order is recorded in
the model itself and in the bundle manifest, so read it rather than typing it:

```{r}
ep <- xgb.load.raw(cfb_ep_model)
getinfo(ep, "feature_name")

cfb_model_manifest$assets[["ep_model.ubj"]]$features
```

## Expected points

The expected points model is a 7-class classifier over the next scoring event.
The manifest's `ep_class_contract` gives the class order and the points each
class is worth; expected points is the probability-weighted sum.

```{r}
contract <- cfb_model_manifest$ep_class_contract
contract$class_order
contract$point_values

# 1st and 10 at the opponent's 25, start of the second half, tied game
play <- data.frame(
  TimeSecsRem = 1800, yards_to_goal = 25, distance = 10,
  down_1 = 1, down_2 = 0, down_3 = 0, down_4 = 0,
  pos_score_diff_start = 0
)
probs <- predict(ep, xgb.DMatrix(as.matrix(play[getinfo(ep, "feature_name")])))
round(setNames(as.vector(probs), contract$class_order), 3)

sum(probs * contract$point_values)
```

## Field goal make probability

The field goal model takes the distance to the goal line plus a one-hot era.
The era cuts are part of the model card, so the encoding comes from the card:

```{r}
era <- cfb_model_cards$fg_model$era_contract
era$buckets

fg <- xgb.load.raw(cfb_fg_model)
kicks <- data.frame(yards_to_goal = c(5, 15, 25, 35, 45))
# a 2024 season falls in the last bucket (>= 2021)
kicks[era$columns] <- as.list(c(0, 0, 0, 1))

data.frame(
  yards_to_goal = kicks$yards_to_goal,
  kick_distance = kicks$yards_to_goal + 17,
  p_make = round(predict(fg, xgb.DMatrix(as.matrix(kicks[getinfo(fg, "feature_name")]))), 3)
)
```

## Model cards

Each model has a card that records what it predicts, how it was trained and on
which seasons:

```{r}
card <- cfb_model_cards$ep_model
card[c("model_type", "objective", "label", "n_features", "training_seasons", "trained_date")]
```

## Where the models come from

The models are the `cfb_model_artifacts` release of
[sportsdataverse-data](https://github.com/sportsdataverse/sportsdataverse-data),
trained by the [sportsdataverse-py](https://py.sportsdataverse.org/) model
pipeline. The same bytes are scored by cfbfastR and sportsdataverse-py, so a
prediction made with sdvmodels matches theirs exactly.
